title: Kicking Off the Yorkshire Challenge at Moortown
content: Started my Yorkshire Golf Challenge at the prestigious Moortown Golf Club in Leeds. A classic parkland course steeped in history — it hosted the 1929 Ryder Cup and has a timeless feel to it. The course was in excellent condition and provided a stern but fair test from the first tee to the 18th green. A fantastic way to kick off the challenge!

title: A Day at the Stunning Rudding Park
content: Rudding Park near Harrogate was an absolute treat. The parkland course winds through beautiful mature trees and the hotel estate grounds, making every hole feel like a proper occasion. The greens were immaculate and the facilities are second to none. Well worth a visit if you are doing the Yorkshire circuit.

title: Summer Golf at Scarcroft
content: A warm summer Sunday at Scarcroft Golf Club just north of Leeds. A well-regarded club with a challenging layout that rewards precise iron play. The views across the Vale of York on the back nine are superb. Great course in fine condition — exactly what you want for a July round.

title: Oulton Hall — Grandeur and Great Golf
content: Playing Oulton Hall feels like stepping back in time. The course is set in the stunning grounds of the Victorian Oulton Hall hotel, giving every round a special atmosphere. The parkland layout is deceptively tricky and the par 3s are particularly memorable. A definite highlight of the challenge so far.

title: A Hidden Gem at Spofforth
content: Spofforth Golf Club is a compact but delightful course tucked away in a quiet North Yorkshire village. A real hidden gem on the Yorkshire golf scene. The welcome was warm, the course was in great shape and the round was thoroughly enjoyable. These smaller clubs are one of the best parts of the challenge.

title: Ganton Golf Club — A True Championship Test
content: Ganton is widely regarded as one of the finest inland courses in England — and after playing it, I completely understand why. The heathland layout is dramatic, the bunkering is severe and the rough demands accuracy off the tee. An absolute bucket-list course. Playing Ganton is a reminder of just how good Yorkshire golf gets.

title: Leeds Golf Club (Cobble Hall) — City Golf at Its Best
content: A pleasant parkland course within the city of Leeds that punches well above its weight. The Cobble Hall course offers a proper test despite its urban surroundings and is always well presented. A great option for a midweek round when you want to stay close to the city.

title: Calverley Golf Club — Friendly and Fun
content: Calverley Golf Club in Pudsey is a friendly, welcoming club with a course that is more challenging than its modest appearance suggests. Some tight tree-lined fairways keep you honest and the greens were rolling beautifully. A cracking afternoon out.

title: Headingley Golf Club — Views to Die For
content: Headingley Golf Club sits high above the city of Leeds and offers stunning panoramic views. On a clear autumn day like this one, you can see for miles. The course itself is a genuine challenge with some tricky uphill and downhill lies. Well worth the walk — in every sense.

title: January Golf at Leeds Golf Centre
content: Braving the Yorkshire winter to tick off the Wike Ridge course at Leeds Golf Centre. The course was cold, damp and windy — perfect Yorkshire winter golf conditions. The layout is open and exposed but the value for money is excellent and the staff were great. Ticking boxes in January feels particularly satisfying.

title: Scarthingwell — A February Surprise
content: Scarthingwell is a lovely parkland course south of Tadcaster that I had been looking forward to visiting. Despite the February conditions, the course was in remarkably good shape. The layout has a nice mix of open and wooded holes that kept the round interesting throughout. A great day out.

title: Alwoodley — One of Yorkshire's Finest
content: Alwoodley Golf Club is a genuine classic — a heathland masterpiece designed by Alister MacKenzie (who also designed Augusta National). Playing here was a real privilege. Every hole feels thoughtfully crafted and the natural beauty of the heathland setting is breathtaking in late May. A course every golfer in Yorkshire should play.

title: Swallow Hall Golf Club
content: A pleasant round at Swallow Hall Golf Club near York. A nicely maintained course with a welcoming atmosphere. Some really interesting holes along the river make for a memorable back nine. Good value and well worth a visit when touring East Yorkshire.

title: The Manor Golf Club — Midsummer Magic
content: Playing The Manor Golf Club in midsummer was an absolute delight. The parkland course was lush and green, and the long evenings meant there was no rush. A course that rewards local knowledge but is welcoming to visiting golfers. Really enjoyed the round.

title: Selby Golf Club — Flat but Rewarding
content: Selby Golf Club sits in the flat landscape south of York and delivers a traditional parkland test. Flat doesn't mean easy though — the course uses its mature trees and water features cleverly to create genuine strategic challenges. A solid day's golf in good company.

title: Cleveland Golf Club — Seaside Flair
content: Cleveland Golf Club near Redcar delivers some links-style coastal golf that makes a refreshing change of scenery. The sea breeze adds an extra challenge to shot selection and the views are stunning. A cracking summer round on the North Yorkshire coast.

title: Cookridge Hall — A West Yorkshire Gem
content: Cookridge Hall is a handsome course set around a hotel complex near Leeds. The parkland layout is mature and the greens were in excellent condition during the late summer visit. Some really characterful holes make this one stand out in the West Yorkshire field.

title: Ending 2024 at Moor Allerton
content: What better way to see out 2024 than a round at the impressive Moor Allerton Golf Club? The Robert Trent Jones Sr-designed course is one of the most unique in Yorkshire, featuring a distinctive open heathland character. Cold, calm and clear — perfect conditions for a New Year's Eve round. Bring on 2025!

title: Sand Moor — Into 2025
content: First round of 2025 and a new course ticked off — Sand Moor Golf Club in Leeds. A heathland course with an Alister MacKenzie pedigree (he advised on the layout), Sand Moor is atmospheric and challenging in equal measure. The sandy subsoil means it drains well and plays well even in January. A great start to the new year.

title: Back-to-Back with Horsforth Golf Club
content: Two days, two new courses! Horsforth Golf Club on the outskirts of Leeds is a classic parkland layout with some wonderfully tricky holes. The elevated tee shots on several holes give great views across the city. The club has a great atmosphere and the greens were putting beautifully.

title: Howley Hall — Spring Has Sprung
content: Spring at Howley Hall Golf Club near Morley was absolutely gorgeous. The parkland was in full bloom and the course was playing at its best. Howley Hall has a loyal membership for good reason — it's a genuinely great golf course. One of the more underrated clubs in West Yorkshire.

title: Knaresborough Golf Club — Taking in the Views
content: Knaresborough Golf Club offers a stunning setting above the town and the River Nidd gorge. The views on several holes are genuinely breathtaking and distract you nicely from the challenge of hitting the fairway. A memorable and enjoyable round in North Yorkshire.

title: Aldwark Manor — Luxury Golf in the Vale of York
content: Aldwark Manor is a beautiful estate course beside the River Ure in the Vale of York. The parkland layout is lush and peaceful, and the manor house hotel provides a wonderful backdrop. A summer round here is an absolute treat — very much a course to bring guests who want to experience Yorkshire golf at its most scenic.

title: The Oaks Golf Club & Spa — A Treat
content: The Oaks near Aughton is a premium parkland experience combining great golf with excellent spa facilities. The course itself is beautifully maintained with some memorable par 3s. A fantastic destination club that is well worth the trip — perfect for a special occasion round.

title: Saltburn by the Sea — Links Golf on the Yorkshire Coast
content: A brilliant day out at Saltburn by Sea Golf Club on the North Yorkshire coast. The clifftop course offers dramatic sea views and classic links-style challenges — firm fairways, tricky winds and small greens that demand a deft short game. The seaside setting makes this one of the most memorable rounds of the challenge so far.

title: Woodhall Hills — Pudsey Parkland
content: Woodhall Hills Golf Club in Calverley is a hidden delight. The parkland layout tumbles across an undulating site giving varied and interesting lies throughout the round. The views west towards Bradford and the Pennines on a clear August day were superb. A great club with a warm welcome.

title: Garforth Golf Club — Late Summer Parkland
content: Wrapped up a busy summer of golf with a round at Garforth Golf Club east of Leeds. A solid parkland course with some really good holes through the trees on the back nine. The course was playing firm and fast in the August sunshine — proper summer golf conditions. Another one in the bag!
